Given that the registration service is made up of multi-tenant ACM hub clusters, we need to determine (for security reasons) if we need to define separate pull secrets for each tenant; or if the global pull secret across all tenants is accetable.

 

The pull secret can be configured for *ks in two different ways:

*Defining a the pull secret in the MultiClusterHub CR:*
[https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.5/html/install/installing#custom-image-pull-secret]

OR

*Using the ManagedClusterImageRegistry to define separate image registeries in a ManagedClusterSet:*
[https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_advanced_cluster_management_for_kubernetes/2.5/html/clusters/managing-your-clusters#imp-clust-custom-image-override]

Since IDP is supported from ACM 2.4+, is it possible to change our placements to {{v1beta1}} so that it doesn't negatively effect other placements in ACM in 2.5+ but still work in 2.4.z? Or have it so that we can create CRDs with either version?

Currently we copy the ManagedCluster Conditions into the RegisteredCluster Conditions.
Some of these Conditions aren't interesting to the RegisteredCluster, like HubAcceptedManagedCluster, and some information isn't readily determined from the conditions alone. 
We expect HAC Dev will want to easily determine:
1. Has the RegisteredCluster been imported yet? Today determined by ManagedClusterConditionJoined.
2. Is the import command ready? Today determined by presence of importCommandRef.
3. ...
We expect GitOps will want to easily determine:
1. Is the kubeconfig secret ready? Today determined by presence of clusterSecretRef.

Should we add more conditions? Or perhaps have a top level field capturing the overall state of the cluster? E.g. Creating, PendingImport, Imported, Ready, Error, etc...

h1. Epic Goal
 * Rapidly take a hot fix to the cloud services:
 ** Code gets checked in, pipeline build, downstream validation
 * WE MEAN HOT FIX PATCH TO EXISTING FUNCTION
 ** We are not delivering new features in this route
 * How _rapid_ is Rapid?
 * CICD's purview:
 ** Post PR merge: Post code change push to pipeline…
 ** Downstream build is ready for handoff to QE
 * Open switches - tradeoffs in quality validation
 ** Can get more rapid via cutting out build VT and handing quickly to downstream QE
 * Managed Services squad awareness
 ** This is culture: being in a ‘hot fix’ ready position 24x7
 ** QE: what level of testing in the context of faster validation
 *** Clear articulation of ‘the PR’ handed to QE for scoped validation
 *** QE needs to be in position to test specifically against the hot fix
 *** QE needs capacity/availability
 **  Engineering has capacity and green light to put hot fix above all else

h2. Why is this important?
 * Cloud Services have an uptime SLA that must be guaranteed

h2. Scenarios
 # Customer encounters issue in cloud service code
 # high priority issue drives alerting to support
 # support triage moves quickly to engineering for evaluation of RCA
 # meanwhile during RCA, code is being updated and readied for PR merge
 # hot fix build verification test is readied
 # hot fix PR and built code is handed to QE for validation
 # new code gets pushed to cloud service

h2. Acceptance Criteria
 * CI - MUST be running successfully with tests automated
 * Release Technical Enablement - Provide necessary release enablement details and documents.
 * Some level of verification test is necessary, what level really is the question.

h2. Dependencies (internal and external)

h2. Open questions::
 # How much QE automation will be in play to verify the fix?
 # Does CICD need to manually roll back other PRs that are in the current build so that a clean hot fix can be built?

When configuring GitHub authentication via Identitatem, we (Operate First) encountered the following scenario:
 - OCP cluster (client) has OAuth via keycloak – using GitHub as underlying idp so, usernames are mapped to github usernames

 - Keycloak converts github usernames to lowercase  

 - All our RBAC in OCP uses these lowercase ocp usernames
 - Switch same cluster Oauth via identitatem – using GitHub as underlying idp
 - Now identitatem maintains character cases in github usernames, so now some OCP usernames are not fully lowercase, invalidating the OCP RBAC (ocp groups seem to be case sensitive)

Example:
{code:java}
~ $ oc whoami
kube:admin

~ $ oc get group cluster-admins -o=jsonpath='{.users[0]}{"\n"}'                   
humairak

~ $ oc login --token=$(pbpaste) --server=https://api.morty.emea.operate-first.cloud:6443  
Logged into "https://api.morty.emea.operate-first.cloud:6443" as "HumairAK" 

~ $ oc whoami
HumairAK

~ $ oc get group cluster-admins -o=jsonpath='{.users[0]}{"\n"}'
Error from server (Forbidden): groups.user.openshift.io "cluster-admins" is forbidden: User "HumairAK" cannot get re
source "groups" in API group "user.openshift.io" at the cluster scope

~ $ 
 {code}
This not an issue for smaller clusters with not that many rbac. But I would imagine for clients with thousands of users with established groups/rbac, this might be cumbersome to update. An option to modify user character case would be useful.
